transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, hello. I guess what brings me in is... this memorial I'm putting together for my brother. It's just gotten a lot bigger than I originally meant it to. 

I've been spending most of my days working on it—chasing down specific songs, calling folks up, planning out these big displays, and organizing trips for it. It's important to me, but my wife is the one who wanted me to come see you. She says I've completely pushed aside the garden, my walking group, and just about everything else I usually do to focus on this. She thinks I'm taking it too far.
Have you found that you need less sleep than usual to feel energized lately?

Well, I wouldn't say that. I've been getting my normal amount of sleep, really. I usually turn in around ten and I'm up by six or so. I haven't noticed any changes there, even with all the work I'm doing on the memorial. I still need a good night's rest to keep going.
Have you felt unusually high, elated, or on top of the world lately?

I guess you could say that. It's kind of a mix, honestly. One minute I'll feel just... lit up, you know? Full of purpose. Like this memorial is going to be the thing that finally makes the whole town understand our family. It feels great, really important. But then... well, if my wife tries to slow me down, or if someone at the senior center questions how I'm doing the displays, I just snap at them. I get really irritable if anyone gets in the way of what I'm trying to do.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt deeply down, depressed, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy for a couple of weeks or more?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, I felt sad when my brother passed, of course, but not... not deeply down or depressed for weeks on end, and I didn't lose interest in things. I've always been pretty steady that way, honestly.
Have you ever had a time in the past when you felt this unusually energized, keyed up, or intensely driven like you do now?

No, I... I don't think so. I've never really had a time like this before. I mean, I worked hard when I was younger, but not quite like this. Feeling this driven, like I just have to get this memorial done and everything has to be perfect... that's new. I haven't ever been keyed up like this in the past.
About how long have you been feeling this intensely driven and working on the memorial like this?
Well, I'd say it's been about two months now. Yeah, right around two months. It started pretty much right after my brother passed away, as soon as I began putting together this tribute for him.
Have you noticed your thoughts moving much faster than usual, like they're racing through your mind?

Yeah, I have noticed that. My mind just keeps jumping from one idea right to the next. One minute I'm thinking about putting together a display case, and then... well, then I'm planning a road trip to track down a cousin, and the next second I'm onto a verse from some old ballad. It just keeps going. I can't even slow it down enough to write it all out in any kind of order.
Have you heard or seen anything unusual lately that other people couldn't hear or see?

Well, yes, I have. Sometimes when I’m sitting at the kitchen table sorting through his old song sheets, I... I hear my brother’s voice. It's clear as day. I'll hear him humming right behind me, or he'll tell me which tune comes next in the pile. Nobody else in the house hears a thing when it happens, just me, but it sounds like he's right there in the room.
